qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Specialized engineering talent, complex infrastructure consulting, and long-standing client relationships, but lack of pricing power in competitive bidding and human-capital intensity limit returns. Erosion threats include procurement price pressure, commoditization of routine design work by AI/BIM automation, and wage inflation for technical talent.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%). Jacobs Solutions operates as a premier global provider of engineering, design, and consulting services for critical infrastructure and water, but historical 10-year median ROIC of ~10.8% falls short of the 12% hurdle. Engineering consulting suffers from competitive procurement pressures, heavy reliance on billable professional hours, and goodwill from serial M&A (e.g. CH2M Hill, PA Consulting), preventing sustained super-normal returns on capital.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 10.8% (FY2022 ~9.2%, FY2023 ~9.8%, FY2024 ~8.1-10.0%, FY2025 ~11.6%), consistently below the 12% threshold across the cycle. Despite successfully spinning off lower-margin government services (CMS and Cyber & Intelligence merged into Amentum in Sept 2024) to streamline into higher-value infrastructure, consulting margins remain capped by competitive bidding and professional staff costs. Operating margins hover in the 8-11% range, and heavy goodwill from past acquisitions dilutes reported invested capital returns.
